timeline_events.summary: The U.S. ambassador met with Saudi Assistant Minister of Defense Prince Khaled bin Sultan to relay concerns about sharing U.S. imagery with Saudi Arabia amid evidence that Saudi aircraft may have struck civilian targets during fighting with Houthi rebels in northern Yemen, and approved the provision of U.S. imagery of the Yemeni border area to the Saudi government after receiving assurances that Saudi Arabia prioritized avoiding civilian strikes.
Thousands marched in Yemen's capital Sanaa calling for President Ali Abdullah Saleh to leave office, in protests over rising poverty and lack of political reform.
Dozens of activists calling for the ouster of Yemen's president Ali Abdullah Saleh clash with government supporters and plainclothes police in Sanaa.
Around 3,000 people protest across southern Yemen in a "Friday of Rage" demanding secession from the north, but heavily deployed security forces quickly stamp out the protests.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh rejects demands to step aside, comparing anti-government protests to a virus, as thousands protest across Yemen and Houthi rebels join demonstrations.
Anti-government protests mount across Yemen for two weeks, leaving President Ali Abdullah Saleh increasingly vulnerable.
Yemen's opposition coalition rejects President Ali Abdullah Saleh's offer to form a national unity government, demanding he step down instead.

Yemeni security forces open fire on anti-government protesters in Harf Sufyan, killing two and injuring nine, as witnesses say three army planes also attack the crowd, while thousands demonstrate against President Ali Abdullah Saleh elsewhere in the country.

The two largest tribal groups in Yemen, the Hashed and the Bakeel, announce their full support for youthful protesters demanding a change of regime, as President Ali Abdullah Saleh rapidly loses control.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh fires the government minister in charge of dialogue with the opposition amid expanding protests against his 32-year rule.

Yemeni troops were deployed across the capital Sanaa as the government tried to quell a new wave of protests against the rule of President Ali Abdullah Saleh, and journalists from three leading American newspapers were deported.

Hundreds of antigovernment protesters clashed with security forces and government supporters in the western port city of Hodeidah, Yemen, where about 10 protesters were shot with live ammunition and hundreds were injured from tear gas and rocks.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh's forces killed at least 46 protesters and wounded hundreds more in the bloodiest single day of the popular uprising, drawing condemnation from the U.N. and the U.S.

More than 50 protesters were gunned down by snipers in Sanaa, Yemen, and tens of thousands of anti-government mourners gathered next to the bodies of activists during a mass funeral procession in the capital.

General Ali Muhsin al-Ahmar, a kinsman of Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh, defects to the opposition amid a flood of high-level resignations, a development described as effectively ending the Saleh regime.
A diplomat and a former minister defect to Yemeni pro-democracy protesters demanding an end to President Ali Abdullah Saleh's 32-year rule.
Insurgents take control of a Yemeni city.
Talks aimed at ending the political standoff in Yemen between President Ali Abdullah Saleh and the opposition have stalled, according to opposition officials.
Yemeni security forces and police in civilian clothes opened fire on anti-government protesters in the southern city of Taiz, killing at least 12 people and injuring scores more.
Saudi Arabia and its Gulf allies are trying to broker a deal for Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh to step down and hand over power, possibly to an interim council of tribal and political leaders.
As uprisings across the Middle East threatened his regime, Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh staged a large pro-government rally in Sanaa.

A WikiLeaks cable reveals that the Yemeni government of President Ali Abdullah Saleh attempted to trick Saudi Arabia into bombing the headquarters of rival General Ali Mohsen al-Ahmar by presenting it as a Houthi rebel base, but the Saudi pilots aborted the strike.

The Gulf Cooperation Council proposes a plan for Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh to transfer powers to his vice president, but opposition leaders reject it because it does not clearly require Saleh to step down.
Six people are killed in a skirmish between rival military factions in Sana'a as hundreds of thousands of anti-regime protesters rally across Yemen.
Rival Yemeni forces clash in the capital Sanaa, killing two people, as the opposition awaits clarification from Gulf Arab mediators on the timeframe for a proposed transfer of the president's powers.
Yemen's opposition sets a two-week deadline for President Ali Abdullah Saleh to step down, rejecting a Saudi-brokered Gulf initiative.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh remains defiant after influential tribal and religious chiefs call for his immediate departure, as nearly 100,000 pro-democracy protesters take to the streets of Sanaa for the eighth consecutive Friday.
Yemenis across disparate groups, including rival tribes, Houthi rebels, and southern separatists, are uniting in protests demanding the ouster of President Ali Abdullah Saleh.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh agrees to step down with conditions, including immunity for himself and his family, after more than three months of pro-democracy protests, though protesters reject the conditions.

Officials say a Gulf Arab-brokered agreement for Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh to give up power could be finalized within a week, as the GCC plans a meeting of Gulf foreign ministers in Riyadh to complete procedures to adopt the initiative.
The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council abruptly leaves a meeting with Yemen's president without reaching a deal, leaving a brokered agreement to end the Yemen crisis on the verge of collapse.

A Gulf-brokered agreement calling for Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh to step down was postponed after Saleh refused to sign it as president, saying he would only ratify it as chairman of the ruling party.
A deal to remove Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh neared collapse after he refused to sign it, raising the threat of more turmoil and violence.
Violence mounts in Yemen after a peace deal stalls.
A Gulf-brokered deal for Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh to resign within a month collapsed after a dispute over who would sign for the opposition, despite U.S. pressure.

Yemen's opposition coalition signed a Gulf Cooperation Council-mediated transition deal to have President Ali Abdullah Saleh step down, while Saleh said he would sign it on Sunday but condemned it as a coup.

Yemeni military helicopters evacuate at least five U.S., European, and Arab ambassadors from the UAE Embassy in Sanaa after hundreds of armed Saleh loyalists block the entrances for hours, as President Saleh stalls at signing a Gulf-mediated deal calling for him to step down in 30 days.

Yemen faces fears of economic collapse and food shortages as political uncertainty and fighting disrupt oil exports and imports, sharply raising food and fuel prices and threatening millions with hunger.
The International Crisis Group calls for an immediate broad cease-fire between President Ali Abdullah Saleh and tribal leaders to prevent wider conflict, as fighting this week killed some 115 people.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh launched air strikes on advancing tribal fighters to prevent the capital Sana'a from falling, as clashes killed more than 120 people and Western leaders urged him to hand over power.

An informal ceasefire between President Ali Abdullah Saleh's security forces and the Hashed tribe led by Sadeq al-Ahmar brings a pause in fighting in Sanaa after nearly a week of deadly clashes that killed some 115 people.
Yemen's trade minister says the political crisis has cost the economy as much as $5 billion and calls for immediate aid to prevent a meltdown.

Street fighting in Yemen's capital Sanaa ended a tenuous ceasefire between tribal groups and forces loyal to President Ali Abdullah Saleh, with explosions, armored vehicles, and missile blasts reported as the country edged closer to civil war.
Clashes in Yemen's capital kill at least 41 people as fighters from the Hasid confederation seize buildings.

Yemen faces a deepening economic crisis amid ongoing political unrest, with fuel and electricity shortages, rising water and food prices, and dwindling foreign currency reserves pushing the country toward economic collapse.
U.S. warplanes launched an airstrike against Al Qaeda targets in southern Yemen, killing midlevel operative Abu Ali al-Harithi and other followers.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh was slightly injured and seven people were killed in a shelling attack on a mosque in the presidential compound, which Saleh blamed on an "outlaw gang" among his tribal enemies.

Yemen's Vice President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi has reportedly taken over as acting president and supreme commander of the armed forces after President Ali Abdullah Saleh was injured in a rocket attack on the presidential palace.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh flew to Saudi Arabia for urgent medical care after being wounded in a rocket attack on his palace, and a cease-fire was announced amid escalating violence.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh is flown to Saudi Arabia for medical treatment, putting Saudi Arabia in a position to influence the outcome of Yemen's crisis.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh, recovering in Saudi Arabia after an attack on his presidential compound, is reported to be making an excellent recovery and could return in the coming days, while opposition leaders move to prevent his return and pressure builds for a power transfer deal.

Yemen’s opposition urges Vice President Abduraboo Mansur Hadi to formally declare that he has assumed the duties of President Ali Abdullah Saleh, who is abroad recovering from injuries, to prevent Saleh from returning to power.
The Obama administration has intensified air strikes on suspected militants in Yemen in a bid to keep them from consolidating power as the government in Sanaa teeters.

U.S. military-led airstrikes in Yemen have resumed after a pause, with the United States believing it probably killed al Qaeda commander Abu Ali al-Harithi, while Yemeni government forces battle militants in the southern town of Zinjibar.

Pro- and anti-regime camps in Yemen stage mass protests urging President Ali Abdullah Saleh to quit after state media said he would soon return from Saudi Arabia, where he is being treated for blast wounds.

Yemen's political opposition holds talks with acting leader Vice President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi in a bid to defuse months of violent political deadlock over the future of President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
More than 60 Islamist militants, including members of an al-Qaeda cell, tunneled out of a prison in the Yemeni port city of Mukalla in a coordinated escape that killed one guard and wounded another.
Southern separatists in Yemen reassert their independence movement amid a power vacuum after President Saleh fled to Saudi Arabia, while Al Qaeda militants seized Zinjibar and displaced thousands.
Yemen's main opposition alliance prepares to discuss forming a transitional council to run the country in place of President Ali Abdullah Saleh, as tens of thousands protest across Yemen.

Yemen's opposition general warns the country is living through a complete political and constitutional stalemate and could be close to civil war, while calling for international intervention to pressure President Saleh.

The top general in the Yemeni opposition, Gen. Ali Mohsen al-Ahmer, rejects a new proposal that would allow embattled President Ali Abdullah Saleh to remain in power until a new leader is found, calling instead for a transfer of power to the vice president and full implementation of the Gulf Cooperation Council agreement.
Pro-government supporters attacked an anti-government protest in Hodeidah, Yemen, killing one protester and injuring more than 150 others, according to witnesses and a medical team member.
A U.S. airstrike on a Yemeni police station overrun by Islamic militants in the town of Mudiya killed at least six fighters.

A coalition of anti-government protest groups in Yemen announces the formation of a 17-member transitional presidential council to lead the country for up to nine months and form a technocrat government once President Ali Abdullah Saleh is toppled.

Tens of thousands of Yemenis protest for and against President Ali Abdullah Saleh's rule in Sanaa as a UN envoy warns of a "catastrophe" and urges a negotiated solution based on a Gulf-brokered transition plan.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh called for an end to months of street protests seeking his ouster and for dialogue with his opponents during Ramadan, while influential tribal leaders announced a coalition to bolster protest demands for his removal.
UNHCR reports a sharp rise in the number of Somali famine victims fleeing to Yemen by boat across the Gulf of Aden, with more than 3,700 refugees reaching Yemen's coast in August.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh was discharged from a Saudi hospital and moved into a government residence in Saudi Arabia, still needing to recuperate before returning to Yemen.
The U.N. Security Council urges Yemeni parties to move forward urgently with an inclusive, orderly, Yemeni-led political transition, and the Yemeni opposition welcomes the call.

Yemen's opposition groups announce the formation of the National Revolution Council, a 143-member body aimed at ending President Ali Abdullah Saleh's regime and seeking recognition as the sole representative of the Yemeni people.
The Yemeni government officially accused opposition figures Hamid al-Ahmar and Ali Mohsen of planning the assassination attempt on President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
Airstrikes killed 36 suspected al-Qaida militants in southern Yemen as the government pressed its campaign against fighters who had overrun several towns.

Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh issued a decree granting his deputy, Abed Rabbo Mansour al-Hadi, authority to negotiate and sign a Gulf Cooperation Council-brokered deal to transfer power, though the decree did not delegate control of the armed forces and the opposition demanded Saleh's commitment to step aside first.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh met with Saudi King Abdullah in Riyadh as clashes between anti-government protesters and security forces in Yemen left almost 50 people dead over two days.

A fragile ceasefire ordered by Yemen's Vice President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi is threatened by renewed shelling in Sanaa, as the death toll from clashes between government forces and troops loyal to defected General Ali Mohsen rises to around 70 since Sunday.
A fragile ceasefire in Yemen breaks as government forces and renegade troops battle in Sana'a, following the shooting deaths of 83 protesters over three days.
Anti-government tribesmen overran a Republican Guards base at Dahrah north of Sanaa, capturing 30 soldiers and killing the base commander, Brig. Ali al-Keleibi.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh says he will leave power in the coming days, but opposition leaders remain skeptical and his government says he will only resign within the framework of the Gulf Initiative.

The U.N. Security Council discusses how to resolve the crisis in Yemen behind closed doors, with no same-day resolution expected, as the U.N. humanitarian chief urges greater world attention to the country.

The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs releases a report warning of a brewing humanitarian crisis in Yemen, with basic commodity costs up 43 percent since January 2011, acute child malnutrition at 40 percent, and over 400,000 people displaced.

Yemeni Nobel laureate Tawakul Karman urged the United Nations to reject a Gulf Arab plan granting immunity to President Ali Abdullah Saleh, as the Security Council circulated a draft resolution urging the plan's implementation while stressing accountability.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh said he is ready to sign a Gulf-brokered deal to step down but demanded American, European Union, and Gulf guarantees on a timetable before signing.

The U.N. refugee agency reports that Somalis fleeing famine and violence are increasingly entering Yemen, straining the country and aid groups, with arrivals rising from an average of 1,600 per month between January and July to 4,500 in August and 3,292 in September.

At least nine people were killed and 23 wounded in clashes between Yemeni security forces and rival fighters in Sanaa, one day after the U.N. Security Council unanimously condemned months of violence in Yemen.
U.N. officials warn that political unrest in Yemen is likely to worsen food shortages and could push the country toward a humanitarian disaster akin to Somalia.
Southern separatists in Yemen, amid growing unrest and a stalled power-transfer deal, say their moment for secession is getting closer as security deteriorates in Aden.
Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh agreed to step down after 33 years in power, with presidential elections set for February 21, 2012.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh said he intends to leave office under a Gulf-brokered power transfer plan, while accusing his opponents of using women and children as human shields.
Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh says he will leave office within 90 days of an agreement with the Gulf Cooperation Council, after months of violent protests demanding he step down.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh signs a Gulf Cooperation Council deal to end his 33-year rule, handing power to his vice president within 30 days and calling for early elections within 90 days, while receiving immunity for himself and his family.
At least 25 people were killed and dozens wounded in northern Yemen in what Sunni Islamist Salafi fighters said was shelling by Shi'ite Muslim rebels on Saturday and Sunday.
Three people were killed in north Yemen when Shi'ite Houthi rebels shelled positions held by Sunni Salafi fighters after the collapse of a week-old cease-fire.
Yemen's vice president calls presidential elections for February 21 under a deal aimed at ending months of protests against President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
Shiite Houthi rebels attack a Sunni Islamist school in northern Yemen, killing more than 20 people and wounding 70 others.
Houthi Shia militants raided a Sunni town in Sa'ada, northern Yemen, killing at least 24 people and injuring 61, with the injured unable to receive medical attention because the town was under siege.

Yemen's vice president names opposition leader Mohammed Basindwa as interim prime minister under a Gulf-sponsored deal aimed at ending months of protests, as violence between Shi'ite rebels and Sunni Islamists in the north kills at least 25 people.
At least 25 people have been killed and dozens wounded in northern Yemen after Shi'ite Houthi rebels shelled Sunni Salafi fighters in Damaj, according to a Salafi spokesman.
Nobel peace laureate Tawakkul Karman urges the International Criminal Court prosecutor to investigate the violent crackdown on dissent in Yemen by President Ali Abdullah Saleh.

Fighting between Shi'ite rebels and Sunni Islamists in north Yemen wounded at least 26 people as the new prime minister worked to form a transitional government under a Gulf plan to ease President Ali Abdullah Saleh from power.

Yemen's vice president announces the formation of a 14-member military council tasked with stabilizing the country and reforming the military, with seats evenly divided between the ruling party and the opposition.
Pro-government forces and tribesmen opposed to Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh traded artillery fire on the streets of the capital Sanaa.
Yemen's vice president announced the formation of a national unity government as part of a power transfer deal to ease President Ali Abdullah Saleh out of power.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo to Tawakkol Karman, a female icon of the protest movement in Yemen, along with two Liberian women.
At least 10 al-Qaida militants escaped from a prison in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden by tunneling out, in the second such jailbreak that year.
Nobel Peace Prize winner Tawakkul Karman demands that Western countries freeze the assets of Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh, criticizing Britain for not acting as it did in Egypt and Tunisia.

At a press conference in Dubai, heads of UN aid agencies appeal to the media to better cover Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis, which the UN says affects more than 8 million people and will continue to rise well into 2012.

Saudi Arabia is stepping up border security along its frontier with Yemen, building watchtowers and installing scanners, as unrest in Yemen drives a wave of migrants, drugs, and weapons into the kingdom.
Sectarian clashes between Shi'ite Houthi rebels and Salafi Sunnis continue in Yemen's northern Saada province, with each side offering conflicting accounts and mediation attempts reaching a dead end.

Foes and backers of a plan to ease Yemen's president out of power fought each other with stones and clubs in Sanaa, injuring at least 20 people, as Washington considered a request from President Ali Abdullah Saleh to fly to the United States for medical treatment.
US drone strikes killed 223 people in Yemen, up from 10 airstrikes in 2011.
Al-Qaeda militants seized control of the Yemeni town of Rada, about 80 miles southeast of Sanaa, overrunning it within hours and pledging allegiance to Ayman al-Zawahiri.
Al Qaeda militants seized full control of the town of Radda, about 100 miles south of Sanaa, overrunning army positions, storming the local prison and freeing at least 150 inmates.

Yemeni officials downplay rumors that next month's presidential elections would be delayed, after the foreign minister hinted at a possible delay due to rising tension, while U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton faulted President Saleh for failing to comply with his commitments.

Outgoing Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh apologizes for "any shortcoming" in his 33-year rule and leaves Yemen for the United States, paving the way for a transfer of power after a year of unrest.
Ali Abdullah Saleh formally stepped down as Yemen’s president after 33 years, with Abed Rabbo Mansour Hadi succeeding him for a transitional period.

Southern separatists in Yemen set fire to a tent camp housing anti-government protesters in the port city of Aden, injuring about 10 people, in opposition to an election to replace outgoing President Ali Abdullah Saleh.

Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi is the only candidate standing to replace Ali Abdullah Saleh as Yemen's next president, facing a collapsing economy, al Qaeda threat, southern secessionism, and northern Houthi rebels.

Yemen holds a single-candidate presidential election in which Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi is chosen to replace Ali Abdullah Saleh, amid separatist violence in the south that killed at least nine people and disrupted voting.
Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi is sworn in as Yemen's new president, formally replacing Ali Abdullah Saleh after a year of protests.
Ali Abdullah Saleh attends a handover ceremony in Yemen, formally ending his 33-year reign as president as power is transferred to Vice President Abdu Rabu Mansur Hadi.
A suicide car bombing targets a Republican Guard troops camp in Bayda, Yemen, killing at least three people including a soldier.

The U.N. High Commissioner on Refugees reports that ongoing tribal clashes in northern Yemen and battles between the military and al-Qaida militants in the south have displaced roughly half a million Yemenis, with 1,800 fleeing their homes in the south in the past two weeks alone.
The World Food Programme says about 5 million people in Yemen, roughly 22% of the population, need emergency food aid, double the 2009 number.
A Swiss teacher was kidnapped by suspected Al Qaeda militants in the Red Sea city of Hodeida and is being held in Yemen's southern Shabwa province.

Former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh says he will not leave Yemen unless his political, tribal, and military foes leave as well, naming Gen. Ali Mohsen and four brothers from the Ahmar family among those who must depart.
A Saudi diplomat, Abdullah al-Khalidi, was abducted by unknown gunmen in Yemen's southern port city of Aden.

Yemen's newly appointed president, Abed Rabbo Mansour Hadi, fired several old-regime figures and relatives of former leader Ali Abdullah Saleh in a major shakeup of the country's military, sacking four governors and more than a dozen military generals.
Almost a quarter of Yemen's population needs urgent food assistance, with malnourished children close to death in hospitals, according to the World Food Program.
The US ambassador to Yemen praises the government's renewed offensive against Al Qaeda, as at least 17 suspected Qaeda militants are killed in an air raid in the south.
Yemeni air force chief Mohammed Saleh al-Ahmar, a relative of former president Ali Abdullah Saleh, resigns, ending a standoff with current president Abd Rabbu Mansour Hadi.

Yemeni government forces recaptured the strategic southern town of Zinjibar from Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula, killed more than 50 militant fighters in recent days, and forced the resignation of an air force commander who had resisted the new leadership's aims.
The White House approved a more aggressive policy allowing "signature" drone strikes in Yemen, expanding the U.S. covert war against AQAP.
Armed militants linked to al-Qaeda stormed a Yemeni military base in Abyan province before dawn, killing at least 20 soldiers and capturing more than two dozen others.

Yemeni separatist activists from the Hirak group describe being approached by Iranian intermediaries and flown to Damascus and Tehran, where Iranian officials offered financial support, infrastructure investment, weapons, and training in exchange for a foothold in southern Yemen, though Iran supported federalism rather than the independence Hirak demands.

The Houthi rebellion in Yemen’s Saada governorate has taken an increasingly sectarian turn and expanded beyond Saada over the past year, with Houthis targeting Salafist religious activities and rejecting the transitional government’s calls to disarm and join the political transition.
At least 32 people, including 23 al Qaeda-linked militants, were killed in Yemen as the government pressed ahead with a U.S.-backed offensive against insurgents in the south.
A suicide bombing in Sanaa, Yemen, killed nearly 100 soldiers and shook the fledgling transition government.
A suicide bomber attacks a military parade in Yemen, killing more than 90 people and wounding at least 220, amid warnings from aid agencies that Yemen faces a food crisis of catastrophic proportions.
Saudi Arabia pledges $3.25bn in aid to Yemen.

Aid groups warn that Yemen's food crisis is reaching catastrophic proportions, with 44 percent of people undernourished and 10 million lacking enough to eat, ahead of the Friends of Yemen conference in Riyadh.
A suicide bomb attack in Sana'a, Yemen, which Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula had been threatening, is cited as a root cause of U.S. counter-terrorism activity in the country.
The Yemeni military continues its offensive against Al-Qaeda militants in the southern Abyan province, backed by American advisers and drones, as fighting intensifies.

Aid agencies warn that 10 million people in Yemen, 44% of the population, are going hungry, with nearly a million children under five suffering acute malnutrition, as the humanitarian crisis worsens amid ongoing conflicts.

The U.S. announced an additional contribution of USAID humanitarian assistance to Yemen, bringing the total U.S. contribution for the year to nearly $80 million, amid a humanitarian crisis in which nearly half the population lacks enough food and nearly 1 million children under 5 are malnourished.
Yemeni troops and al-Qaeda fighters engage in ongoing street battles and guerrilla warfare on the frontline in Zinjibar, the capital of Abyan province, with artillery, tanks, and sniper fire.

Yemen's military launches airstrikes against al-Qaeda-linked Islamist fighters in the southern province of Abyan, bombing a weapons cache east of Jaar, as residents and aid agencies report that a month-old offensive has cut off food and medicine supplies.

Aid agencies warn that almost half of Yemen's population of 25 million do not have enough food to eat, with a third of children in some areas severely malnourished, and Oxfam and Islamic Relief issue a joint appeal for $38m as UN funding remains only 48% met.
A U.S. drone strike in Yemen killed a cleric who had preached against al-Qaida, along with his cousin and three militants, fueling anti-American sentiment.

Yemen faces its worst-ever humanitarian crisis, with 10 million people going hungry and more than five million in urgent need of assistance as skyrocketing food and fuel prices make Ramadan the hardest year ever.

Hundreds of Republican Guard forces loyal to former Yemeni president Ali Abdullah Saleh encircled the Defense Ministry in Sanaa for several hours, protesting a move to strip the ex-president's son of part of his military command.
Clashes erupted in Yemen's capital between the new government's forces and soldiers loyal to the former regime, highlighting ongoing tensions six months after President Ali Abdullah Saleh's ouster.

Houthi rebels in Yemen expanded their public presence in Sanaa through posters, banners, and graffiti denouncing the United States, signaling growing influence after being confined by former President Saleh.

A U.S. airstrike killed 12 civilians, including two cousins of Ahmed Saleh Ahmed al-Duqari, near the town of Radda, Yemen, amid allegations that the Yemeni government is trying to cover up the attack.

A U.S. airstrike, initially claimed by the Yemeni government as its own attack on al-Qaida militants, killed 11 civilians traveling in a truck near Radda, Yemen, with survivors and officials later saying the victims were all civilians.
International donors pledge $6.4 billion in aid to Yemen at a donor conference in Riyadh to support its transition to democracy amid a humanitarian and security crisis.
International donors led by the UK pledge $6.4bn in aid to Yemen to address its deepening humanitarian crisis and underpin its economy.

Anti-US protests spread to the US Embassy in Sanaa, Yemen, driven by anger over civilian deaths from drone strikes and a settlement granting former president Ali Abdullah Saleh immunity, rather than solely by an anti-Islam film.
Yemeni President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi signs a decree authorizing the creation of a commission of inquiry to investigate human rights violations during the 2011 uprising.

Families in poverty-stricken Yemen are increasingly being forced to marry off their young daughters so they can afford food, as the country faces a hunger catastrophe with an estimated 10 million people not having enough to eat.

At the Friends of Yemen meeting in New York, the international community pledged nearly $1.5bn in additional funding to support Yemen's transition, following $6.4bn in pledges made at a Riyadh donors' conference earlier in the month.

Eight international and Yemeni aid agencies call for more targeted emergency funding to address Yemen's hunger crisis, which affects 10 million people, ahead of the Friends of Yemen donor conference in New York.
Houthi rebels are seen gaining new influence in Yemen, expanding their presence in Sanaa through posters, banners, and graffiti denouncing the United States.

Southern Yemeni separatist leaders have returned from exile to rally support for reviving the state of South Yemen, exploiting weakened central authority and a freer political atmosphere since the 2011 uprising that ousted President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
Yemen's only liquefied natural gas terminal resumed exports after its feed pipeline was blown up in late September.
Al-Qaeda loyalists launched an attack on a military base in the southern town of Shuqra, Yemen, killing at least 15 soldiers and wounding scores of others.
An expert says Iran is backing Yemeni militants, including the Houthis, to increase its regional influence and potentially control the Bab El-Mandeb Strait.
Four Shiite Houthi Muslims were killed and 10 others wounded in an explosion at a worship site in Sanaa during a religious festival.
Gunmen killed a Saudi diplomat and his Yemeni bodyguard in Sanaa.

Yemeni President Abd Rabbu Mansour Hadi issued decrees reorganizing the armed forces to fold units commanded by allies of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh into a four-branch army under his command as commander-in-chief.
Yemen's security chief, Major-General Ali al-Ahmadi, accused Iran of training and funding Shi'ite Houthi rebels in northern Yemen and called on Tehran to stop interfering.
A Yemeni military court sentenced 93 members of the Republican Guard to prison terms of up to seven years for an August attack on a military complex in Sanaa, while acquitting five others.

Yemeni President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi announces the restructuring of the army and defence ministry, scrapping the elite Republican Guard commanded by former President Ali Abdullah Saleh's oldest son Ahmed and dismissing other Saleh loyalists.

Brigadier-General Ahmed Ali Abdullah Saleh, son of Yemen's former president, agreed to transfer missiles under his command to President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi after his elite Republican Guard was disbanded.

The United Arab Emirates announces the arrest of a suspected militant cell in a joint operation with Saudi Arabia, with Dubai's police chief later saying some members were affiliated with al Qaeda in Yemen.
Dozens of armed Yemeni tribesmen protest in the southern town of Redaa against U.S. drone strikes, which they say have killed innocent civilians.
Saudi Arabia's foreign minister denies a newspaper report that the kingdom's air force, rather than U.S. drones, carried out some strikes on al Qaeda targets in Yemen.
Dubai's police chief says a suspected militant cell detained in the United Arab Emirates had links to al Qaeda, including its Yemen-based wing AQAP.
US drone strikes killed nine suspected al Qaeda members in Yemen's Marib province, including local al Qaeda chief Ismail bin Jamil and Hamad Hassan Ghreib.
A U.S. drone airstrike on a vehicle east of Yemen's capital Sanaa killed three suspected al-Qaida militants and wounded two others.
U.N. agencies and international aid groups jointly appeal for at least $716 million to address Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis, including widespread malnutrition.
A UN Security Council delegation begins a brief visit to Yemen to support President Abdrabuh Mansur Hadi and help resolve problems hampering national reconciliation talks.

Yemen announced the seizure of a weapons cache, including surface-to-air missiles and explosives, from a ship in Yemeni territorial waters in the Arabian Sea, with a U.S. official saying markings indicate the weapons came from Iran and were believed headed for Shiite insurgents in Yemen.
Yemen's president asks Iran's president to stop backing armed groups on Yemeni soil after coastguards seized a consignment of missiles and rockets believed sent by Iran.

The UN Security Council warns Yemen's former president Ali Abdullah Saleh and former vice president Ali Salim Al-Beidh that they could face possible sanctions for interfering in the country's democratic transition and undermining the national unity government.
Yemeni police shot dead two activists in Aden during clashes with protesters calling for southern independence on the first anniversary of Ali Abdullah Saleh's ouster.

Yemeni troops shot dead a southern separatist and wounded two others in Aden during clashes that erupted when activists from the separatist Southern Movement blocked roads and burned tyres in a campaign of civil disobedience.

Yemeni authorities freed two separatist leaders, Qassem Askar and Hussein bin Shouaib, in response to southern demands, and exiled southern leader Ahmed Bin Farid al-Suraimi returned to Aden after nearly two decades abroad.
UN envoy to Yemen Jamal Benomar is set to meet Southern Movement leaders in Dubai ahead of a national dialogue scheduled to begin on March 18, which some separatists aim to boycott.
A national dialogue aimed at drawing up a new constitution and preparing for elections is set to start in Sanaa.
Residents of Aden stage a general strike called by southern separatists protesting the start of Yemen's national dialogue.
Yemen launches a UN-backed national dialogue aimed at national reconciliation, though hardline southern factions boycott the talks and stage protests and a general strike in Aden.

Yemen opens a six-month national dialogue in Sanaa aimed at drafting a new constitution and preparing for February 2014 elections, as police shoot dead a protester in southern Yemen demonstrating against the talks.
Yemen’s National Dialogue is scheduled to start, though the country’s overall security remains under threat.
A member of Yemen's al-Harak secessionist movement declares at a national dialogue conference that southern Yemen has the right to independence, drawing applause.
Gunmen shot dead three people in a failed assassination attempt on Houthi rebel leader Abdo Abu Ras as he returned to his hotel in Sanaa after leaving Yemen's national dialogue talks.
Yemenis yearn for Arab Spring success but fear a proxy conflict between Riyadh and Tehran.

facts.text: On 2011-01-27, thousands marched in Yemen's capital Sanaa calling for President Ali Abdullah Saleh to leave office, in protests over rising poverty and lack of political reform.

On 2011-03-18, Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh's forces killed at least 46 protesters and wounded hundreds more in the bloodiest single day of the popular uprising, drawing condemnation from the U.N. and the U.S.

On 2011-04-11, the Gulf Cooperation Council proposed a plan for Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh to transfer powers to his vice president, but opposition leaders rejected it because it did not clearly require Saleh to step down.
On 2011-05-02, a deal to remove Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh neared collapse after he refused to sign it, raising the threat of more turmoil and violence.

On 2011-06-04, Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh flew to Saudi Arabia for urgent medical care after being wounded in a rocket attack on his palace, and Vice President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi reportedly took over as acting president.

On 2011-11-23, Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh signed a Gulf Cooperation Council deal to end his 33-year rule, handing power to his vice president within 30 days and receiving immunity for himself and his family.
On 2012-02-25, Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi was sworn in as Yemen's new president, formally replacing Ali Abdullah Saleh after a year of protests.

On 2012-12-19, Yemeni President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi announced restructuring of the army and defence ministry, scrapping the elite Republican Guard commanded by former President Saleh's oldest son Ahmed and dismissing other Saleh loyalists.

event-eff20ae82f4f8563.summary: Yemen's vice president announced the formation of a national unity government as part of a power transfer deal to ease President Ali Abdullah Saleh out of power.

event-cfb74ed4ecc6d41b.summary: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo to Tawakkol Karman, a female icon of the protest movement in Yemen, along with two Liberian women.

event-1f320e2d10c9468c.summary: At least 10 al-Qaida militants escaped from a prison in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden by tunneling out, in the second such jailbreak that year.

event-d0133fbe1caf5967.summary: Nobel Peace Prize winner Tawakkul Karman demands that Western countries freeze the assets of Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh, criticizing Britain for not acting as it did in Egypt and Tunisia.

event-2956eb2464dc2022.summary: At a press conference in Dubai, heads of UN aid agencies appeal to the media to better cover Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis, which the UN says affects more than 8 million people and will continue to rise well into 2012.

event-6783caf197403c71.summary: Saudi Arabia is stepping up border security along its frontier with Yemen, building watchtowers and installing scanners, as unrest in Yemen drives a wave of migrants, drugs, and weapons into the kingdom.

event-e065318b77437952.summary: Sectarian clashes between Shi'ite Houthi rebels and Salafi Sunnis continue in Yemen's northern Saada province, with each side offering conflicting accounts and mediation attempts reaching a dead end.

event-673ab93c3d907899.summary: Foes and backers of a plan to ease Yemen's president out of power fought each other with stones and clubs in Sanaa, injuring at least 20 people, as Washington considered a request from President Ali Abdullah Saleh to fly to the United States for medical treatment.

event-a7d9efafcd68daf4.summary: US drone strikes killed 223 people in Yemen, up from 10 airstrikes in 2011.

event-7236a2a7d594605c.summary: Al-Qaeda militants seized control of the Yemeni town of Rada, about 80 miles southeast of Sanaa, overrunning it within hours and pledging allegiance to Ayman al-Zawahiri.

event-d2ae75c588f8f783.summary: Al Qaeda militants seized full control of the town of Radda, about 100 miles south of Sanaa, overrunning army positions, storming the local prison and freeing at least 150 inmates.

event-4e9baa64659c6fc9.summary: Yemeni officials downplay rumors that next month's presidential elections would be delayed, after the foreign minister hinted at a possible delay due to rising tension, while U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton faulted President Saleh for failing to comply with his commitments.

event-9a9a0da3749db207.summary: Outgoing Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh apologizes for "any shortcoming" in his 33-year rule and leaves Yemen for the United States, paving the way for a transfer of power after a year of unrest.

event-b0a1038dc1ff75c6.summary: Ali Abdullah Saleh formally stepped down as Yemen’s president after 33 years, with Abed Rabbo Mansour Hadi succeeding him for a transitional period.

event-2988c95c650e10ef.summary: Southern separatists in Yemen set fire to a tent camp housing anti-government protesters in the port city of Aden, injuring about 10 people, in opposition to an election to replace outgoing President Ali Abdullah Saleh.

event-b74804ee79a2a6aa.summary: Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi is the only candidate standing to replace Ali Abdullah Saleh as Yemen's next president, facing a collapsing economy, al Qaeda threat, southern secessionism, and northern Houthi rebels.

event-3107b5564a241ac8.summary: Yemen holds a single-candidate presidential election in which Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi is chosen to replace Ali Abdullah Saleh, amid separatist violence in the south that killed at least nine people and disrupted voting.

event-8459412332c116fd.summary: Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi is sworn in as Yemen's new president, formally replacing Ali Abdullah Saleh after a year of protests.

event-f4a057fd4dddafbf.summary: Ali Abdullah Saleh attends a handover ceremony in Yemen, formally ending his 33-year reign as president as power is transferred to Vice President Abdu Rabu Mansur Hadi.

event-1f28a1862cff828d.summary: A suicide car bombing targets a Republican Guard troops camp in Bayda, Yemen, killing at least three people including a soldier.

event-1ba7822d826bbf71.summary: The U.N. High Commissioner on Refugees reports that ongoing tribal clashes in northern Yemen and battles between the military and al-Qaida militants in the south have displaced roughly half a million Yemenis, with 1,800 fleeing their homes in the south in the past two weeks alone.

event-68bd61276c1607ae.summary: The World Food Programme says about 5 million people in Yemen, roughly 22% of the population, need emergency food aid, double the 2009 number.

event-c21beb5620444cf4.summary: A Swiss teacher was kidnapped by suspected Al Qaeda militants in the Red Sea city of Hodeida and is being held in Yemen's southern Shabwa province.

event-a9b4536e062c1620.summary: Former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh says he will not leave Yemen unless his political, tribal, and military foes leave as well, naming Gen. Ali Mohsen and four brothers from the Ahmar family among those who must depart.

event-ccc1bd0c948a863c.summary: A Saudi diplomat, Abdullah al-Khalidi, was abducted by unknown gunmen in Yemen's southern port city of Aden.

event-a98eb6ce62fb02a3.summary: Yemen's newly appointed president, Abed Rabbo Mansour Hadi, fired several old-regime figures and relatives of former leader Ali Abdullah Saleh in a major shakeup of the country's military, sacking four governors and more than a dozen military generals.

event-5aacbe04a5b6b613.summary: Almost a quarter of Yemen's population needs urgent food assistance, with malnourished children close to death in hospitals, according to the World Food Program.

event-9750750ac5c87043.summary: The US ambassador to Yemen praises the government's renewed offensive against Al Qaeda, as at least 17 suspected Qaeda militants are killed in an air raid in the south.

event-8a7eac0f25303081.summary: Yemeni air force chief Mohammed Saleh al-Ahmar, a relative of former president Ali Abdullah Saleh, resigns, ending a standoff with current president Abd Rabbu Mansour Hadi.

event-b4416a9fa2cfa04e.summary: Yemeni government forces recaptured the strategic southern town of Zinjibar from Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula, killed more than 50 militant fighters in recent days, and forced the resignation of an air force commander who had resisted the new leadership's aims.

event-bfd7f94dfbb32c66.summary: The White House approved a more aggressive policy allowing "signature" drone strikes in Yemen, expanding the U.S. covert war against AQAP.

event-e7df4ca3526e1eb6.summary: Armed militants linked to al-Qaeda stormed a Yemeni military base in Abyan province before dawn, killing at least 20 soldiers and capturing more than two dozen others.

event-232452decf28f126.summary: Yemeni separatist activists from the Hirak group describe being approached by Iranian intermediaries and flown to Damascus and Tehran, where Iranian officials offered financial support, infrastructure investment, weapons, and training in exchange for a foothold in southern Yemen, though Iran supported federalism rather than the independence Hirak demands.

event-9308bd44bd376da4.summary: The Houthi rebellion in Yemen’s Saada governorate has taken an increasingly sectarian turn and expanded beyond Saada over the past year, with Houthis targeting Salafist religious activities and rejecting the transitional government’s calls to disarm and join the political transition.

event-9bc8950b1fad3480.summary: At least 32 people, including 23 al Qaeda-linked militants, were killed in Yemen as the government pressed ahead with a U.S.-backed offensive against insurgents in the south.

event-99ffd0fdb795cfa2.summary: A suicide bombing in Sanaa, Yemen, killed nearly 100 soldiers and shook the fledgling transition government.

event-a236bddf39e57c3e.summary: A suicide bomber attacks a military parade in Yemen, killing more than 90 people and wounding at least 220, amid warnings from aid agencies that Yemen faces a food crisis of catastrophic proportions.

event-199e271262ed2522.summary: Saudi Arabia pledges $3.25bn in aid to Yemen.

event-83aac18257d6d0aa.summary: Aid groups warn that Yemen's food crisis is reaching catastrophic proportions, with 44 percent of people undernourished and 10 million lacking enough to eat, ahead of the Friends of Yemen conference in Riyadh.

event-66cfe2691f534c6a.summary: A suicide bomb attack in Sana'a, Yemen, which Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula had been threatening, is cited as a root cause of U.S. counter-terrorism activity in the country.

event-a8db12c5ce93147b.summary: The Yemeni military continues its offensive against Al-Qaeda militants in the southern Abyan province, backed by American advisers and drones, as fighting intensifies.

event-e2f66958e73ffe2d.summary: Aid agencies warn that 10 million people in Yemen, 44% of the population, are going hungry, with nearly a million children under five suffering acute malnutrition, as the humanitarian crisis worsens amid ongoing conflicts.

event-a4b75bb778b5100d.summary: The U.S. announced an additional contribution of USAID humanitarian assistance to Yemen, bringing the total U.S. contribution for the year to nearly $80 million, amid a humanitarian crisis in which nearly half the population lacks enough food and nearly 1 million children under 5 are malnourished.

event-22ab0e7b5000c6cf.summary: Yemeni troops and al-Qaeda fighters engage in ongoing street battles and guerrilla warfare on the frontline in Zinjibar, the capital of Abyan province, with artillery, tanks, and sniper fire.

event-4fcb0d91123c70d6.summary: Yemen's military launches airstrikes against al-Qaeda-linked Islamist fighters in the southern province of Abyan, bombing a weapons cache east of Jaar, as residents and aid agencies report that a month-old offensive has cut off food and medicine supplies.

event-a2e83bff159b3f39.summary: Aid agencies warn that almost half of Yemen's population of 25 million do not have enough food to eat, with a third of children in some areas severely malnourished, and Oxfam and Islamic Relief issue a joint appeal for $38m as UN funding remains only 48% met.

event-c52e8dfff84f8a55.summary: A U.S. drone strike in Yemen killed a cleric who had preached against al-Qaida, along with his cousin and three militants, fueling anti-American sentiment.

event-3170f4e01fc30631.summary: Yemen faces its worst-ever humanitarian crisis, with 10 million people going hungry and more than five million in urgent need of assistance as skyrocketing food and fuel prices make Ramadan the hardest year ever.

event-c0037da6c080ec23.summary: Hundreds of Republican Guard forces loyal to former Yemeni president Ali Abdullah Saleh encircled the Defense Ministry in Sanaa for several hours, protesting a move to strip the ex-president's son of part of his military command.

event-494dfc840a077d3f.summary: Clashes erupted in Yemen's capital between the new government's forces and soldiers loyal to the former regime, highlighting ongoing tensions six months after President Ali Abdullah Saleh's ouster.

event-ad0573fcb12d3e64.summary: Houthi rebels in Yemen expanded their public presence in Sanaa through posters, banners, and graffiti denouncing the United States, signaling growing influence after being confined by former President Saleh.

event-5dcdbc83a0b7355c.summary: A U.S. airstrike killed 12 civilians, including two cousins of Ahmed Saleh Ahmed al-Duqari, near the town of Radda, Yemen, amid allegations that the Yemeni government is trying to cover up the attack.

event-f6a00bd7841b798b.summary: A U.S. airstrike, initially claimed by the Yemeni government as its own attack on al-Qaida militants, killed 11 civilians traveling in a truck near Radda, Yemen, with survivors and officials later saying the victims were all civilians.

event-a07a1dca83f13e86.summary: International donors pledge $6.4 billion in aid to Yemen at a donor conference in Riyadh to support its transition to democracy amid a humanitarian and security crisis.

event-44ef5d61dcf7a7a7.summary: International donors led by the UK pledge $6.4bn in aid to Yemen to address its deepening humanitarian crisis and underpin its economy.

event-ce7422c562aa29af.summary: Anti-US protests spread to the US Embassy in Sanaa, Yemen, driven by anger over civilian deaths from drone strikes and a settlement granting former president Ali Abdullah Saleh immunity, rather than solely by an anti-Islam film.

event-743197bca89eb2bc.summary: Yemeni President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi signs a decree authorizing the creation of a commission of inquiry to investigate human rights violations during the 2011 uprising.

event-25fa96a9868cc777.summary: Families in poverty-stricken Yemen are increasingly being forced to marry off their young daughters so they can afford food, as the country faces a hunger catastrophe with an estimated 10 million people not having enough to eat.

event-4d79722cbb3b2a6d.summary: At the Friends of Yemen meeting in New York, the international community pledged nearly $1.5bn in additional funding to support Yemen's transition, following $6.4bn in pledges made at a Riyadh donors' conference earlier in the month.

event-87b9d3b3310f1479.summary: Eight international and Yemeni aid agencies call for more targeted emergency funding to address Yemen's hunger crisis, which affects 10 million people, ahead of the Friends of Yemen donor conference in New York.

event-72dc8b481892b389.summary: Houthi rebels are seen gaining new influence in Yemen, expanding their presence in Sanaa through posters, banners, and graffiti denouncing the United States.

event-7880204aff3f4aea.summary: Southern Yemeni separatist leaders have returned from exile to rally support for reviving the state of South Yemen, exploiting weakened central authority and a freer political atmosphere since the 2011 uprising that ousted President Ali Abdullah Saleh.

event-fc462a11c749c8ee.summary: Yemen's only liquefied natural gas terminal resumed exports after its feed pipeline was blown up in late September.

event-7a237c6a17c5c046.summary: Al-Qaeda loyalists launched an attack on a military base in the southern town of Shuqra, Yemen, killing at least 15 soldiers and wounding scores of others.

event-29c6bb4b760c43e6.summary: An expert says Iran is backing Yemeni militants, including the Houthis, to increase its regional influence and potentially control the Bab El-Mandeb Strait.

event-9efe1b76ffe4f2f9.summary: Four Shiite Houthi Muslims were killed and 10 others wounded in an explosion at a worship site in Sanaa during a religious festival.

event-0f680d13fec83d53.summary: Gunmen killed a Saudi diplomat and his Yemeni bodyguard in Sanaa.

event-78dbf55cbd2e91e6.summary: Yemeni President Abd Rabbu Mansour Hadi issued decrees reorganizing the armed forces to fold units commanded by allies of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh into a four-branch army under his command as commander-in-chief.

event-167b818c690bb0fe.summary: Yemen's security chief, Major-General Ali al-Ahmadi, accused Iran of training and funding Shi'ite Houthi rebels in northern Yemen and called on Tehran to stop interfering.

event-e1a5ef122a647d15.summary: A Yemeni military court sentenced 93 members of the Republican Guard to prison terms of up to seven years for an August attack on a military complex in Sanaa, while acquitting five others.

event-1c51c32b66048373.summary: Yemeni President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi announces the restructuring of the army and defence ministry, scrapping the elite Republican Guard commanded by former President Ali Abdullah Saleh's oldest son Ahmed and dismissing other Saleh loyalists.

event-a870b5170790cf33.summary: Brigadier-General Ahmed Ali Abdullah Saleh, son of Yemen's former president, agreed to transfer missiles under his command to President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi after his elite Republican Guard was disbanded.

event-de78c66b313e8675.summary: The United Arab Emirates announces the arrest of a suspected militant cell in a joint operation with Saudi Arabia, with Dubai's police chief later saying some members were affiliated with al Qaeda in Yemen.

event-3b48eec3a19ed66b.summary: Dozens of armed Yemeni tribesmen protest in the southern town of Redaa against U.S. drone strikes, which they say have killed innocent civilians.

event-be2871cd64e4b208.summary: Saudi Arabia's foreign minister denies a newspaper report that the kingdom's air force, rather than U.S. drones, carried out some strikes on al Qaeda targets in Yemen.

event-fea1567e1e84f56e.summary: Dubai's police chief says a suspected militant cell detained in the United Arab Emirates had links to al Qaeda, including its Yemen-based wing AQAP.

event-3a60dc9570a8ce64.summary: US drone strikes killed nine suspected al Qaeda members in Yemen's Marib province, including local al Qaeda chief Ismail bin Jamil and Hamad Hassan Ghreib.

event-8cbca93a856cb8d8.summary: A U.S. drone airstrike on a vehicle east of Yemen's capital Sanaa killed three suspected al-Qaida militants and wounded two others.

event-91a9f86a2bf69b97.summary: U.N. agencies and international aid groups jointly appeal for at least $716 million to address Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis, including widespread malnutrition.

event-ca68bc709f6aedd0.summary: A UN Security Council delegation begins a brief visit to Yemen to support President Abdrabuh Mansur Hadi and help resolve problems hampering national reconciliation talks.

event-a834cf43f4c6249b.summary: Yemen announced the seizure of a weapons cache, including surface-to-air missiles and explosives, from a ship in Yemeni territorial waters in the Arabian Sea, with a U.S. official saying markings indicate the weapons came from Iran and were believed headed for Shiite insurgents in Yemen.

event-14ba0848fe2e7fde.summary: Yemen's president asks Iran's president to stop backing armed groups on Yemeni soil after coastguards seized a consignment of missiles and rockets believed sent by Iran.

event-54d0538bde30afe5.summary: The UN Security Council warns Yemen's former president Ali Abdullah Saleh and former vice president Ali Salim Al-Beidh that they could face possible sanctions for interfering in the country's democratic transition and undermining the national unity government.

event-7c42ccd70d62ab25.summary: Yemeni police shot dead two activists in Aden during clashes with protesters calling for southern independence on the first anniversary of Ali Abdullah Saleh's ouster.

event-6cf45ae1c0be36da.summary: Yemeni troops shot dead a southern separatist and wounded two others in Aden during clashes that erupted when activists from the separatist Southern Movement blocked roads and burned tyres in a campaign of civil disobedience.

event-6855dac4ef2a680c.summary: Yemeni authorities freed two separatist leaders, Qassem Askar and Hussein bin Shouaib, in response to southern demands, and exiled southern leader Ahmed Bin Farid al-Suraimi returned to Aden after nearly two decades abroad.

event-c003effce114dc61.summary: UN envoy to Yemen Jamal Benomar is set to meet Southern Movement leaders in Dubai ahead of a national dialogue scheduled to begin on March 18, which some separatists aim to boycott.

event-e334caec1880befe.summary: A national dialogue aimed at drawing up a new constitution and preparing for elections is set to start in Sanaa.

event-58b329f88c21825a.summary: Residents of Aden stage a general strike called by southern separatists protesting the start of Yemen's national dialogue.

event-9dd44b1737faae55.summary: Yemen launches a UN-backed national dialogue aimed at national reconciliation, though hardline southern factions boycott the talks and stage protests and a general strike in Aden.

event-19191082bb118b67.summary: Yemen opens a six-month national dialogue in Sanaa aimed at drafting a new constitution and preparing for February 2014 elections, as police shoot dead a protester in southern Yemen demonstrating against the talks.

event-9e593df731f15a65.summary: Yemen’s National Dialogue is scheduled to start, though the country’s overall security remains under threat.

event-81b9a2844db20d52.summary: A member of Yemen's al-Harak secessionist movement declares at a national dialogue conference that southern Yemen has the right to independence, drawing applause.

event-b629f08030803138.summary: Gunmen shot dead three people in a failed assassination attempt on Houthi rebel leader Abdo Abu Ras as he returned to his hotel in Sanaa after leaving Yemen's national dialogue talks.

event-e2b46615d0faf62b.summary: Yemenis yearn for Arab Spring success but fear a proxy conflict between Riyadh and Tehran.

event-1a01ba69225e01ae.summary: Yemen's ousted president Ali Abdullah Saleh arrived in Saudi Arabia for medical tests, with a government aide saying he should remain in exile because his presence provokes separatists and rebels.

event-5edd8b82823e75cc.summary: Yemen's future remains unclear as the National Dialogue Conference and international talks continue following the uprising that forced President Ali Abdullah Saleh from office after 33 years.

event-d11dcb9eaa65be7d.summary: Yemen's Ministry of Fisheries Wealth announces the closing of the shrimp fishing season in Yemen's Red Sea regional waters from April 15, 2013 until further notice.

event-34da9463959f6353.summary: A Finnish couple and an Austrian student abducted in Yemen in December 2012 were freed by local tribesmen near the Omani border and handed over to Omani authorities.

event-714f0348de98c949.summary: Three employees of the International Committee of the Red Cross were kidnapped by Yemeni tribesmen in the city of Jaar, Abyan province, and are reported to be in good condition while negotiations for their release continue.

event-4dcaf89abe1cfb5d.summary: A Yemeni Guantanamo Bay detainee says he feels abandoned by President Barack Obama and the world after more than 10 years at the U.S. prison, as the administration continues to prohibit transfers of detainees to Yemen.

event-d7f41aac84312b79.summary: The US attorney general Eric Holder hints that the Obama administration may be planning to act on Yemeni prisoners held at Guantánamo Bay, saying the block on sending cleared Yemeni detainees back to Yemen is under review.

event-81d4deffb8efa33c.summary: A senior United Nations aid official warns that Yemen's humanitarian crisis could cause its Arab Spring political transition to collapse, noting that more than half of Yemen's 24 million people need aid and that the UN's aid effort is severely underfunded.

event-4f6bcf62b61b10d9.summary: A suspected U.S. drone strike killed four suspected Al Qaeda militants and destroyed explosives they were carrying in the Al-Mahfad region of Abyan province, Yemen, also injuring several others.

event-141469e6fc9812c6.summary: The United States lifted its ban on transferring Guantanamo detainees to Yemen, a country that had been blocked from receiving detainees since January 2010.

event-34b61221618b009d.summary: Attackers blew up Yemen's main oil export pipeline in Maarib province, halting the flow of crude.

event-7419ad7027d3a892.summary: Yemen's human rights minister appeals to the United States and Gulf Arab countries to help fund a $20 million rehabilitation centre for Yemenis released from Guantanamo Bay prison.

event-650d02d612b7e20b.summary: Tens of thousands of Yemeni Shi'ite Muslims buried the remains of Hussein al-Houthi, founder of the armed Houthi rebel group, nine years after he was killed in fighting with government forces.

event-8f9c42cc4280bfda.summary: Yemen begins the second round of its UN-backed national dialogue in Sanaa, aimed at drafting a new constitution and preparing for 2014 elections.

event-48f0a36a13015f47.summary: At least seven people are killed and at least 30 wounded in a gun fight as Shia Houthi rebels attack the National Security Agency building in Sanaa, Yemen, with automatic weapons and grenades while demanding the release of political detainees.

event-19d67a32900d0674.summary: The Syrian opposition charged that Shiite Zaidi rebels from Yemen have joined the fight alongside Assad’s troops, a claim Zaidis denied.

event-7f733de432ef2d37.summary: Yemen’s National Dialogue Conference is preparing for its second general plenary to discuss initial committee drafts, while key committees remain paralyzed by disputes and the southern issue threatens the dialogue’s success.

event-ba4d4c92ff578cf8.summary: Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula confirms that its deputy leader Saeed al-Shehri was killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

event-86c7e77b0084be5e.summary: Yemen is mentioned as one of the unfettered arms markets supplying weapons to Hamas in Gaza, according to Israeli military intelligence officials cited in a classified 2009 State Department cable.

events.summary: Al-Qaeda loyalists launched an attack on a military base in the southern town of Shuqra, Yemen, killing at least 15 soldiers and wounding scores of others.
Yemen begins the second round of its UN-backed national dialogue in Sanaa, aimed at drafting a new constitution and preparing for 2014 elections.
Tens of thousands of Yemeni Shia Muslims buried the remains of Hussein al-Houthi, founder of the armed Houthi rebel group, nine years after he was killed in fighting with government forces.
Four Shiite Houthi Muslims were killed and 10 others wounded in an explosion at a worship site in Sanaa during a religious festival.
Talks aimed at ending the political standoff in Yemen between President Ali Abdullah Saleh and the opposition have stalled, according to opposition officials.
Yemen’s National Dialogue is scheduled to start, though the country’s overall security remains under threat.
Tens of thousands of Yemeni Shi'ite Muslims buried the remains of Hussein al-Houthi, founder of the armed Houthi rebel group, nine years after he was killed in fighting with government forces.
Violence mounts in Yemen after a peace deal stalls.
Gunmen shot dead three people in a failed assassination attempt on Houthi rebel leader Abdo Abu Ras as he returned to his hotel in Sanaa after leaving Yemen's national dialogue talks.
Yemen launches a UN-backed national dialogue aimed at national reconciliation, though hardline southern factions boycott the talks and stage protests and a general strike in Aden.
Tens of thousands of Yemeni Shi'ite Muslims buried the remains of Hussein al-Houthi, founder of the armed Houthi rebel group, nine years after he was killed in fighting with government forces.
Clashes erupted in Yemen's capital between the new government's forces and soldiers loyal to the former regime, highlighting ongoing tensions six months after President Ali Abdullah Saleh's ouster.

A coalition of anti-government protest groups in Yemen announces the formation of a 17-member transitional presidential council to lead the country for up to nine months and form a technocrat government once President Ali Abdullah Saleh is toppled.

Yemen’s opposition urges Vice President Abduraboo Mansur Hadi to formally declare that he has assumed the duties of President Ali Abdullah Saleh, who is abroad recovering from injuries, to prevent Saleh from returning to power.

events.summary: At a press conference in Dubai, heads of UN aid agencies appeal to the media to better cover Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis, which the UN says affects more than 8 million people and will continue to rise well into 2012.
The World Food Programme says about 5 million people in Yemen, roughly 22% of the population, need emergency food aid, double the 2009 number.
International donors led by the UK pledge $6.4bn in aid to Yemen to address its deepening humanitarian crisis and underpin its economy.
U.N. officials warn that political unrest in Yemen is likely to worsen food shortages and could push the country toward a humanitarian disaster akin to Somalia.

A senior United Nations aid official warns that Yemen's humanitarian crisis could cause its Arab Spring political transition to collapse, noting that more than half of Yemen's 24 million people need aid and that the UN's aid effort is severely underfunded.

Aid groups warn that Yemen's food crisis is reaching catastrophic proportions, with 44 percent of people undernourished and 10 million lacking enough to eat, ahead of the Friends of Yemen conference in Riyadh.
UNHCR reports a sharp rise in the number of Somali famine victims fleeing to Yemen by boat across the Gulf of Aden, with more than 3,700 refugees reaching Yemen's coast in August.
Yemen hopes for international aid at a "Friends of Yemen" donors meeting in New York, as the U.N. warns the country is on the verge of a humanitarian crisis.

Eight international and Yemeni aid agencies call for more targeted emergency funding to address Yemen's hunger crisis, which affects 10 million people, ahead of the Friends of Yemen donor conference in New York.
U.N. agencies and international aid groups jointly appeal for at least $716 million to address Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis, including widespread malnutrition.
International donors pledge $6.4 billion in aid to Yemen at a donor conference in Riyadh to support its transition to democracy amid a humanitarian and security crisis.

The U.N. refugee agency reports that Somalis fleeing famine and violence are increasingly entering Yemen, straining the country and aid groups, with arrivals rising from an average of 1,600 per month between January and July to 4,500 in August and 3,292 in September.
Yemen's human rights minister appeals to the United States and Gulf Arab countries to help fund a $20 million rehabilitation centre for Yemenis released from Guantanamo Bay prison.

The US attorney general Eric Holder hints that the Obama administration may be planning to act on Yemeni prisoners held at Guantánamo Bay, saying the block on sending cleared Yemeni detainees back to Yemen is under review.

Three employees of the International Committee of the Red Cross were kidnapped by Yemeni tribesmen in the city of Jaar, Abyan province, and are reported to be in good condition while negotiations for their release continue.

A Saudi activist from Jazan Province, detained two weeks earlier after calling for protests over the displacement of families near the border with Yemen and the jailing of prisoners, begins a hunger strike to protest his detention without a court hearing date.
The United States lifted its ban on transferring Guantanamo detainees to Yemen, a country that had been blocked from receiving detainees since January 2010.
A Finnish couple and an Austrian student abducted in Yemen in December 2012 were freed by local tribesmen near the Omani border and handed over to Omani authorities.
At least 10 al-Qaida militants escaped from a prison in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden by tunneling out, in the second such jailbreak that year.
Yemeni security forces opened fire on a crowd of Houthi protesters outside the National Security Bureau headquarters in Sanaa, killing 13 people and wounding as many as 100.
More than 60 Islamist militants, including members of an al-Qaeda cell, tunneled out of a prison in the Yemeni port city of Mukalla in a coordinated escape that killed one guard and wounded another.

A Yemeni Guantanamo Bay detainee says he feels abandoned by President Barack Obama and the world after more than 10 years at the U.S. prison, as the administration continues to prohibit transfers of detainees to Yemen.

Yemeni military helicopters evacuate at least five U.S., European, and Arab ambassadors from the UAE Embassy in Sanaa after hundreds of armed Saleh loyalists block the entrances for hours, as President Saleh stalls at signing a Gulf-mediated deal calling for him to step down in 30 days.
A Swiss teacher was kidnapped by suspected Al Qaeda militants in the Red Sea city of Hodeida and is being held in Yemen's southern Shabwa province.

A coalition of anti-government protest groups in Yemen announces the formation of a 17-member transitional presidential council to lead the country for up to nine months and form a technocrat government once President Ali Abdullah Saleh is toppled.

The U.N. Security Council condemns Syrian government forces in the strongest possible terms for heavy-weapon and close-range attacks on the town of Houla that killed 108 people, including 34 children, while stopping short of directly blaming anyone and as the Syrian government denies responsibility.

Yemen's vice president announces the formation of a 14-member military council tasked with stabilizing the country and reforming the military, with seats evenly divided between the ruling party and the opposition.

Yemeni officials downplay rumors that next month's presidential elections would be delayed, after the foreign minister hinted at a possible delay due to rising tension, while U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton faulted President Saleh for failing to comply with his commitments.
Yemen's vice president calls presidential elections for February 21 under a deal aimed at ending months of protests against President Ali Abdullah Saleh.
The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council abruptly leaves a meeting with Yemen's president without reaching a deal, leaving a brokered agreement to end the Yemen crisis on the verge of collapse.
The U.N. Security Council urges Yemeni parties to move forward urgently with an inclusive, orderly, Yemeni-led political transition, and the Yemeni opposition welcomes the call.

A group of young Yemeni protesters says it has set up a 17-member transitional council to manage the country's affairs, though a senior leader of Yemen's largest opposition bloc says his group will not accept the council and at least one named member says he had no prior knowledge of it.
Yemeni opposition groups and protest leaders form a national council to step up pressure on President Ali Abdullah Saleh to relinquish power.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh fled to Saudi Arabia for medical treatment after being wounded in a rocket attack on his presidential compound, amid months of protests calling for his ousting.

Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh agrees to step down with conditions, including immunity for himself and his family, after more than three months of pro-democracy protests, though protesters reject the conditions.
Yemeni official powers are transferred to the vice president after an attack on President Saleh, amid a Saudi-brokered cease-fire.

Airstrikes killed 36 suspected al-Qaida militants in southern Yemen as the government pressed its campaign against fighters who had overrun several towns.
At least 32 people, including 23 al Qaeda-linked militants, were killed in Yemen as the government pressed ahead with a U.S.-backed offensive against insurgents in the south.

U.S. military-led airstrikes in Yemen have resumed after a pause, with the United States believing it probably killed al Qaeda commander Abu Ali al-Harithi, while Yemeni government forces battle militants in the southern town of Zinjibar.

International donors led by the UK pledge $6.4bn in aid to Yemen to address its deepening humanitarian crisis and underpin its economy.
Saudi Arabia's foreign minister denies a newspaper report that the kingdom's air force, rather than U.S. drones, carried out some strikes on al Qaeda targets in Yemen.

Gunmen killed a Saudi diplomat and his Yemeni bodyguard in Sanaa.
